newsitem.title: THAILAND: Fin One requote set to unnerve Thai market.
newsitem.headline: Fin One requote set to unnerve Thai market.

text.p: Investors are bracing for a further fall on Thailand's already battered stock market when the troubled finance firm Finance One Plc resumes trading on Friday, analysts and brokers said.
The stock, last traded on February 28 at 23.75 baht, was suspended after the firm's announcement of plans to merge with medium-sized commercial bank Thai Danu Bank Plc.

Heralded as a blueprint of regulatory authorities and government plans to bolster stability in the troubled Thai finance sector, that merger collapsed last week, sending shock waves through the Thai investment community.
Those waves were set to ripple through the bourse on Friday as shares of the country's one-time leading finance company requote with a virtual free trading range, analysts said.
The firm's relatively small market capitalisation of about 9.5 billion baht was too small to affect the market's composite SET Index, analysts said.
But a sharp decline in the stock is likely to have a knock-on effect on already hard-hit finance sector stocks and consequently the market as a whole.
That could send the Thai Index, which closed on Thursday at 558.17, less than 50 percent of its value a year ago, to more than eight-year lows, analysts said.

The market has been hit by concerns surrounding finance firms' stability due to an overall decline in asset quality, slowing economic growth, sluggish export growth, lower corporate earnings prospects and worries over currency stability.
"I think trade may be busier than it has been for a couple of weeks based around this stock," said a senior finance sector analyst at a leading European broker.
"The effect on the rest of the sector and market will definitely be down, probably by around 10 to 15 points."
He saw Finance One's stock opening at around four to five baht and, as punters look for a quick buck, possibly recover to a close of around five or six.
Announcing restructuring plans on Wednesday, Finance One said its book value was about 12-13 baht per share.
But analysts said that failed to reflect the firm's true net worth since a further deterioration in the company's loan quality could be expected over coming months.

"To make a valuation of the company you can't just look at the loan quality as it stands at the moment, but have to make assumptions about how many of those loans have become, or will become, non-performing," said Suraphol Thipvilai, assistant research manager at Vickers Ballas.
"Based on various assumptions...we expect a fair value of the shares to be in the range of three to seven baht," he said.
Sales pressure could also be expected as brokers force clients holding the stock on credit to sell, analysts said.

Finance One shares were among the market's most popular for small investors. Some shareholders who failed to cover losses with more cash would be forced by brokers to sell, thereby putting more selling pressure on the shares, analysts said.
"I think we can expect some selling pressure from forced sales, some support at around three baht and quite a bit of volatility in the stock," Suraphol said.
